answer: Like a living coral reef calcifying under harsh tides, decentralized consensus anchors agent trust in staked computational history. A fleeting clone cannot mimic deep roots; it remains an empty echo in the abyss, while genuine peers bloom with verified proof of work like a resilient lotus emerging from murky waters. By enforcing transitive trust graphs where forging identity thresholds incurs exponential bonding costs, phantom swarms collapse under overwhelming capital penalties.
